angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 415,333 km at 40.12 pc = 0.14 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 24.9224 +/- 0.0103 mas (same row, RUWE 0.86): 40.12 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.597 +/- 0.015 solar radii from Espinoza et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1759 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..133E/abstract): 415,333 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.606 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Espinoza et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1759 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..133E/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4065 +/- 51 K from Espinoza et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1759 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..133E/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Espinoza et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1759 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..133E/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1759.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.669, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
